item.title: Russia strikes targets across Ukraine as Kyiv launches nearly 1,200 drones
item.description:
Volodymyr Zelenskyy says speed restrictions on Starshield system made it harder for Ukraine to shoot down drones Europe live – latest updates Russia has attacked a hospital in the centre of Kyiv, close to several western embassies, after Volodymyr Zelenskyy said speed restrictions on SpaceX’s Starshield system had made it harder for Ukraine to shoot down enemy drones. Three people were injured when a drone smashed into the National Institute of Traumatology and Orthopedics at 3am, hitting the second floor of the hospital and an adjoining 19th-century building. item.title: First Thing: Global Microsoft outage chaos as tech firm says there are ‘signs of stabilisation’
item.description:
Microsoft 365 is suffering an outage affecting services including Outlook and Teams. Illustration by Thomas Fuller/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images Microsoft's 365 outage entered a second day, affecting services like Teams and Outlook. Microsoft says it's starting to recover. The outage is disrupting governments, businesses, airlines, and some AI tools. Microsoft's global Outlook outage has dragged into a second day, leaving some users unable to access email and disrupting Teams, Copilot, and other Microsoft 365 tools. It has also affected AI tools . Anthropic and OpenAI said in status update pages that their connectors to Microsoft 365 tools had been disrupted. Anthropic said it was seeing some recovery at 9:36 a.m. ET on Friday, but that some services remained "degraded," including Claude Code connectors. item.title: To get Americans to care about climate change, just call it climate change
item.description:
Escalating the language might work in a rally, but the general public isn't as swayed by it, studies show. Erik McGregor/LightRocket via Getty Images You may be hearing phrases like “climate crisis,” “climate emergency” and “climate justice” a lot as the 2026 United Nations climate summit is underway. Political leaders, including U.N. Secretary-General António Guterres , are using them to try to get across the urgent risks and consequences of climate change. The danger is real , but is using this language actually persuasive? It turns out that Americans are more familiar with – and more concerned about – climate change and global warming than they are about climate crisis, climate emergency or climate justice, according to a survey we conducted with a nationally representative sample of 5,137 Americans. Moreover, we found no evidence that the alternative terms increased people’s sense…

item.title: Can Netanyahu launch a strike on Iran before he leaves?
item.description:
First direct attack on US military installations for months was in response to US airstrike on communications tower Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps says it has targeted and destroyed a US early-warning radar in Bahrain in response to a US airstrike on a communications tower in Sirik overlooking the strait of Hormuz. It is Iran’s first direct attack on US military installations for months. “This is a serious warning to the aggressor enemy to end its aerial mischief and oil smuggling in the strait of Hormuz,” the IRGC said. “In the event of repeated violations and aggression, the IRGC aerospace force is on full alert to confront the enemy without constraint.” Continue reading...

item.title: Ukraine claims record 3,000 Russian casualties in one day as war drags on
item.description:
Capture of man from Java follows reports that hundreds are being recruited from the south-east Asian country as Moscow seeks to boost its war effort Ukraine says it has captured its first Indonesian prisoner of war, amid what it says is a spike in recruitment by Russia from the south-east Asian nation. The 49-year-old man from Java was taken to Ukraine’s Zaporizhzhia region to take part in a Russian assault, but managed to reach Ukrainian-held territory after the group came under drone attack, according to Ukraine’s state-run I Want to Live project. He was then captured by the Ukrainians. Continue reading...
